identificationEvidence.title: TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report
identificationEvidence.scope: Actual PDF printed and physical pages 9: The report explicitly identifies Penateka as a historical Comanche band and prints the three selected variants in the same paragraph. Its stated historical range includes the Edwards Plateau and central Texas river headwaters. Historical name/relationship check only; no present-government or present-membership claim.

identificationEvidence.title: TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report
identificationEvidence.scope: Actual PDF printed and physical pages 9: The report explicitly calls Nokoni a band, prints Nokoninvv, and describes north Texas to New Mexico. It also groups Nokoni with the separately named Tanima and Tenawa as Middle Comanche; that collective label is not adopted as an exact alias for Nokoni. Historical name/relationship check only; no present-government or present-membership claim.

identificationEvidence.title: TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report
identificationEvidence.scope: Actual PDF printed and physical pages 9: The report explicitly names Kotsoteka and the two printed variants in its historical-band discussion, locating the account in present-day western Oklahoma along the Canadian River. Historical name/relationship check only; no present-government or present-membership claim.

identificationEvidence.title: TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report
identificationEvidence.scope: Actual PDF printed and physical pages 9, 10: The report names Yamparika and four printed variants as a historical Comanche band. Its range sentence crosses the page break and names the Arkansas River; the passage does not resolve a particular modern state for this outline. Historical name/relationship check only; no present-government or present-membership claim.

identificationEvidence.title: TxDOT Tribal Histories: Comanche Nation Research Report
identificationEvidence.scope: Actual PDF printed and physical pages 10: The report names Quahadi as the fifth band in this historical summary, prints Quahada and Kwaharv, and explicitly connects its Llano Estacado account to eastern New Mexico and the Texas Panhandle. Historical name/relationship check only; no present-government or present-membership claim.

limits: Historical band outlines add no substantive works and imply no current separate governments.
Yamparika retains an explicit regional review gap; no state is inferred from Arkansas River.
